subject: Pilot pricing: smoothing minimums & persistent-context amortization proposal
messages:

Subject: Pilot pricing: smoothing minimums & persistent-context amortization proposal

Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I put together a short pilot pricing proposal that tries to address BrightCart's two main asks: (1) avoid noisy invoice surprises from per-call minimums during microbursts, and (2) ensure long-context agents don't get double-charged when the conversation persists across multiple requests.

High-level summary of what we're proposing for the 90-day pilot:
- Smoothing window: per-account call volumes under 250 calls/day will be aggregated into a 4-hour smoothing window to coalesce microbursts; billing is calculated on aggregated token units within that window instead of per-call minima.
- Persistent-context amortization: for long-agent sessions (context > 16k tokens), we amortize the initial ingest tokens across subsequent requests from the same conversation id for up to 72 hours, capped at 10x the initial amortization baseline.
- Pilot concession: 10% off list for the duration, and a one-time goodwill credit to align the first invoice if rounding pushes over expected spend.

Attached: brightcart_pilot_pricing_sample.csv (sample invoice calculations using your reported traffic profile) and brightcart_requirements.docx (notes from discovery).

Questions for you so we can finalize:
1) Does BrightCart want the smoothing window applied at the org-account level or per-environment (prod/stage)?
2) Any constraints from procurement on amortization caps (e.g., maximum amortization period < 72 hours)?
3) Who should sign the SOW — Sarah or Procurement? We can prep a DocuSign link once terms are agreed.

If you want, Kimberly can drop in a short worked example next email showing three sample sessions and the invoice delta with smoothing vs without.

Thanks,
Michael Grant

Michael —

Thanks — this looks promising and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side before we loop procurement: 

1) Aggregation level: we prefer the smoothing window at the org-account level (we operate a single production org with multiple merchants and want the smoothing to prevent merchant-level microburst surprises).
2) Amortization cap: procurement flagged the 72-hour cap as potentially long — they asked whether we can split the difference and start with 48 hours for the pilot. The main objective is to avoid recharging the full ingest tokens on every follow-up message in a short-lived session.
3) Invoice visibility: procurement asked that any goodwill credit be shown as a separate line item and that you provide a short worked calc for them to attach to the PO.

We'll need an SOW and an invoice sample to pass to our finance team. Once Procurement signs off on the 48-hour cap, they will be happy to review a concise SOW + DocuSign link.

Can you and Kimberly produce a 3-session worked example (prod-level traffic profile, org-level smoothing window, 48h amortization) showing the invoice impact? That should be enough to move to PO.

—Sarah

Sarah / team —

Thanks for the quick feedback, Sarah. Attached is a short worked example (kb-smoothing-calcs.pdf) — three sessions modeled using the traffic numbers you shared during discovery. I ran the math both with the 4-hour smoothing window at org-level and with a 48-hour amortization cap as requested. Key takeaways: 

- Example A (short sessions with frequent microbursts): smoothing reduces invoice line-item volatility by ~42% vs per-call minima, while absolute delta vs raw per-token billing is only ~6% for the month.
- Example B (few long-agent sessions): amortization at 48h captures ~78% of re-use benefits of the 72h proposed cap while limiting potential over-amortization.
- Rounding behavior: we apply per-invoice-line rounding to the nearest billing quantum (10 token unit) after aggregation; the pilot goodwill credit will only be applied if rounding causes >$250 delta vs expected pilot run-rate.

Notes on implementation: we will tag calls with your org id + conversation id. Amortization runs off a short-lived KV cache that persists keys for the chosen amortization window. This is compatible with both Hosted and Dedicated deployments; no code changes required on your side.

I've attached the calc PDF and included the CSV sample Michael attached with annotated columns. If you want, I can also export a spreadsheet that line-by-line maps to your example invoices.

Kimberly Park
